name: Miami Gardens City Council

meetings.pattern: Second and fourth Wednesday of each month, 5:30 p.m., City Hall Council Chambers, 18605 NW 27th Avenue, Miami Gardens, FL 33056

schedule.note: City Council Regular Meeting, Council Chambers

phases.name: Second budget hearing, FY 2026-27 budget and final millage adopted
phases.decides: Final millage rate and the city budget for the fiscal year starting October 1, 2026, adopted at a special council meeting starting 5:01 p.m. in Council Chambers.

phases.name: Fiscal year begins
phases.decides: The adopted budget and millage take effect for October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027.

phases.name: Candidate qualifying for the August 2026 city election
phases.decides: Who appears on the ballot for Residential Seats 2 and 4 and At-Large Seat 6; qualifying ran 9 a.m. Monday April 13 to 4 p.m. Wednesday April 15, 2026 at the Clerk's office, Suite 317.

phases.name: City general election (held with the state primary)
phases.decides: Council Seats 2, 4 and 6, four-year terms. Polls 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

phases.name: City runoff, Residential Area Seat 4
phases.decides: Runoff between Mykita Cherry-Prime and Rod Mack for Seat 4; early voting October 19 to November 1, 2026 at county early voting sites.

levers.how: Speak during the Public Comments item on the regular council agenda. For the September 2026 budget hearing the city asked speakers to pre-register by emailing the City Clerk; for the CRA special meeting the same day it required registration at least one hour before the meeting.
levers.rules: Time limit and sign-up rule for regular meetings not found on any fetchable city page (CivicWeb agenda portal blocks automated fetches). Budget hearing notice: 'ALL interested parties are invited to attend and will be heard'; pre-register with the City Clerk by email.
levers.deadline: At least one hour before the meeting for pre-registration, per the Sept 23, 2026 CRA notice; confirm for regular meetings

levers.how: Email the City Clerk, Mario Bataille, at mbataille@miamigardens-fl.gov. Regular agendas also carry an item for 'Written requests, petitions and other written communications from the public'.
levers.rules: No posted rule on how written comments are read into the record. Email address as printed on the city clerk page; the budget hearing notice printed it with a typo.

levers.how: Email any of the seven council members directly; addresses follow the pattern first initial plus last name at miamigardens-fl.gov (rharris, rstephens, kbaskin, pwilson, mpowell, lporter, ljulien). Main line 305-622-8000.
levers.rules: City Hall hours 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Thursday.

levers.how: The City Clerk is the records custodian; requests go through the Public Records page or the clerk's office.

Charter amendment by citizen petition is available under state law: a petition signed by 10 percent of the registered electors as of the last municipal general election forces a referendum at the next general election or a special election.
levers.rules: Fla. Stat. 166.031(1) (state law floor). The city charter's own initiative and referendum sections could not be read: the city's charter PDF is a scan with no text layer and municode.com and the CivicWeb portal block automated fetches. Section numbers and any city-specific thresholds are not recorded here.

levers.how: Same as petition above; the charter's referendum section (if any) was not readable. Charter amendments proposed by the council or a charter revision commission go to the voters; the charter revision commission is in Charter Section 6.2.
levers.rules: Charter Sec. 6.2 (charter revision commission) confirmed only from a 2014 ballot question; full text not read.

levers.how: Recall of a council member follows Florida's uniform municipal recall statute, which applies to every city whether or not its charter has a recall section. For a city with 25,000 or more electors, the first petition needs the greater of 1,000 electors or 5 percent, gathered within 30 days; a second 'Recall Petition and Defense' round needs 15 percent within 60 days. A member elected only by a residential area is recalled only by that area's electors.
levers.rules: Fla. Stat. 100.361(1), (2)(b), (2)(f), (3)(a), (3)(c), (11), (12). Petitions are filed with the City Clerk.
levers.deadline: 30 days for the first round of signatures; 60 days for the second

levers.how: File candidate paperwork with the City Clerk, who is the Supervisor of Municipal Elections. The 2026 window was 9 a.m. April 13 to 4 p.m. April 15.
levers.rules: Candidates must file forms with the City Clerk before opening a campaign account. The next qualifying period (for the 2028 election) is not yet posted.

levers.how: City general elections are held in even years on the state primary date; runoffs on the state general election date. The Seat 4 runoff is November 3, 2026.
levers.rules: Registered Miami Gardens voters; Seat 4 runoff is limited to Residential Area 4 voters.

levers.how: The city has advisory boards (Citizen Advisory Board, Keep Miami Gardens Beautiful, Historic Advisory Committee) that meet at City Hall or the BTF Complex; application details were not found on a fetchable page.

elections.terms: Four years. Mayor and two council members elected at large; four council members elected by Residential Area. General election every even year on the state primary date, runoff on the state general election date. The 2026 cycle covered Seats 2, 4 and 6; the Mayor and the other seats come up in 2028.

contacts.name: Mario Bataille (direct line on election notice)

Agenda lead days unknown.
